typical.note: Board, not chip. Raspberry Pi documentation, "Power supply" section (source file power-supplies.adoc), table "Typical power requirements": Zero 2 W "Typical bare-board active current consumption" 350mA (recommended PSU 2A).

peak.note: No Raspberry Pi stress figure for the Zero 2 W. Scaled from the Pi 4B in the same documentation (Stress Max 1.25 A / bare-board 600 mA = 2.08): 0.35 A x 2.08 = 0.73 A, rounded to 0.75 A. The Pi 3B (same BCM2837 family) ratio is higher (Stress Max 1.34 A / bare-board 400 mA = 3.35, giving 1.17 A) but the Pi 3B has an on-board USB hub and Ethernet and was measured with Wi-Fi, keyboard and mouse; the lower ratio was taken. Board, not chip.
peak.label: CPU stress

minVolts.note: Not documented. The 3V3 rail is a PAM2306 buck (U3, L1 4.7 uH): below about 3.3 V plus its P-MOSFET drop it runs at 100 % duty and VOUT = VIN - ILOAD (RDS(ON) + RL), RL the inductor DC resistance (PAM2306 "100% Duty Cycle Operation", p. 11; RDS(ON) P MOSFET 0.3 ohm typ, p. 4), so 3V3 falls out of regulation from about 3.4 V in. 3.5 V taken as the brown-out point. The Zero range has no 4.63 V low-voltage detection (power-supplies.adoc).

ron.note: Zero 2 W reduced schematic: micro-USB J1 (690-005-298-486) pin 1 VBUS goes straight to the 5V net (C1 47u, test points PP1 and PP70); no fuse, diode or switch in series. 10 mohm stands for the connector and copper (assumed; not measured).

vout.note: U3 on the Zero 2 W reduced schematic is a PAM2306AYPKE (Diodes Inc.); its ordering code (p. 13) gives Output Voltage V1 "K: 3.3V", V2 "E: 1.8V". Channel 1 (LX1, L1 4.7 uH, FB1 to the output) drives the 3V3 net.

efficiency.note: Read from PAM2306 "Efficiency VS Output Current (Vo=3.3V)" (p. 5), VIN = 5 V curve, L = 4.7 uH: about 80 % at 30 mA, about 88 % at 100 mA, about 92 % at 200 to 500 mA, about 88 % at 1 A. 0.88 for tens to hundreds of mA.

vinMin.note: The PAM2306 input range is 2.5 to 5.5 V (p. 4), but as a buck it cannot hold 3.3 V below about VOUT plus the P-MOSFET drop (100 % duty, p. 11; RDS(ON) 0.3 ohm typ at 100 mA, p. 4): 3.3 V + 0.2 A x 0.3 ohm = 3.36 V, rounded to 3.4 V. This solver holds vout across vinMin..vinMax, so vinMin is set where regulation ends, not the chip's 2.5 V.

vinMax.note: chip, not board. PAM2306 Electrical Characteristics (p. 4): Input Voltage Range 2.5 to 5.5 V.

ioutMax.note: chip, not board. PAM2306 Features (p. 1): "Output Current: Up to 1A per Channel". No 3.3 V header budget is documented for the Zero 2 W; the channel also feeds the board's own 3.3 V loads (RP3A0 I/O, wireless).

outputResistance.note: BCM2835/6/7 and RP3A0 table in gpio-on-raspberry-pi.adoc. At maximum drive (16 mA): IOL min 18 mA at VO = 0.4 V, 0.4 / 0.018 = 22 ohm; IOH min 17 mA at VO = 2.3 V, (3.3 - 2.3) / 0.017 = 59 ohm. The default is 8 mA (reset DRIVE = 3, gpio-pad-controls.adoc), half the parallel drivers of 16 mA, so about 44 and 118 ohm, mean 81, rounded to 80 ohm. Within the default-drive limits of the same table: VOL max 0.14 V and VOH min 3.0 V at 2 mA give at most 70 and 150 ohm. Chip, not board.

pullup.note: gpio-on-raspberry-pi.adoc, table for BCM2835, BCM2836, BCM2837 and RP3A0-based products: RPU pull-up resistor min 50, max 65 kohm, no typical; midpoint taken. Chip, not board.

pulldown.note: Same table: RPD pull-down resistor min 50, max 65 kohm, no typical; midpoint taken. Chip, not board.

inputLeakage.note: chip, not board. gpio-on-raspberry-pi.adoc, BCM2835/6/7 and RP3A0 table: IIL input leakage current max 5 uA at TA = +85 C.

inputLow.note: chip, not board. gpio-on-raspberry-pi.adoc, BCM2835/6/7 and RP3A0 table: VIL input low voltage max 0.9 V. One source.

inputHigh.note: chip, not board. gpio-on-raspberry-pi.adoc, BCM2835/6/7 and RP3A0 table: VIH input high voltage min 1.6 V (hysteresis enabled). One source.

ohms.note: Board value. Zero 2 W reduced schematic: R23 1.8K 1% on GPIO2 and R24 1.8K 1% on GPIO3, both to 3V3.
Board value. Zero 2 W reduced schematic: R23 1.8K 1% on GPIO2 and R24 1.8K 1% on GPIO3, both to 3V3.

notes: Board: Zero 2 W reduced schematic https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rpizero2/raspberry-pi-zero-2-w-reduced-schematics.pdf (2021): micro-USB J1 VBUS -> 5V net -> U3 PAM2306AYPKE dual buck (channel 1 3V3 via L1 4.7 uH, channel 2 1V8 via L2 2.2 uH); U16 RT8088AWSC makes VDD_CORE from the 5V_CORE net. Header J8 pins 2 and 4 are on the same 5V net.

SoC: RP3A0 system-in-package with a BCM2710A1 die (product brief https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rpizero2/raspberry-pi-zero-2-w-product-brief.pdf, PDF p. 2). GPIO figures come from the Raspberry Pi documentation table "for BCM2835, BCM2836, BCM2837 and RP3A0-based products" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/documentation/master/documentation/asciidoc/computers/raspberry-pi/gpio-on-raspberry-pi.adoc).

The Zero range has no 4.63 V low-voltage detection: power-supplies.adoc, "Power supply warnings": "On all models of Raspberry Pi since the Raspberry Pi B+ (2014) except the Zero range, there is low-voltage detection circuitry ...".
PAM2306 offPath "open": "During shutdown, the input is disconnected from the output" (p. 1). Reverse "body-diode": not documented; the high-side P-MOSFET body diode runs from the switch node to VIN.
No iq on the 3V3 rail: the board draw is a whole-board figure and already includes it (PAM2306 quiescent 40 uA typ per channel, p. 4).
GPIO pins: GPIO2 to GPIO27; GPIO0 and GPIO1 (ID_SD, ID_SC) are the HAT ID EEPROM pins and stay out. The header is unpopulated on the Zero 2 W (product brief).
unaccounted: USB devices on the micro-USB data port (USB OTG): the documentation gives no budget ("Limited by PSU, board, and connector ratings only."); not simulated.
The camera (CSI) connector: the Camera Module needs about 250 mA (power-supplies.adoc), not in the board draw.
HATs and anything else powered from the 5V or 3V3 header pins beyond the user circuit the sheet draws: the board draw covers the board only.
Mini-HDMI output (about 50 mA per power-supplies.adoc) and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth transmit bursts are not separated from the bare-board figure.
